newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees '96 world cereal output 1.821 bln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees '96 world cereal output 1.821 bln tonnes.

text.p: The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation said its latest forecast for 1996 world cereal production was 1.821 billion tonnes.

The Rome-based agency said in its Food Outlook that the output forecast was 5.2 percent up from 1995's reduced level but the supply and demand situation had changed little since it issued its last report in June.
The latest forecast is slightly down from the 1.828 billion tonnes seen in the last outlook in June.

"Latest information on the 1996 cereal crops continues to point to a recovery in world production after the sharply reduced harvest last year," FAO said. "But the global supply/demand situation will remain tight in 1996/97."
FAO said that, assuming favourable conditions until harvest, global output of wheat was forecast to increase by 4.8 percent to 571 million tonnes.
Coarse grain output was seen increasing by 7.6 percent to 875 million tonnes while rice was seen at 375 million tonnes (milled), marginally above last year's levels.

FAO said that at the forecast level of output, aggregate world cereal production would be large enough to meet expected consumption needs in 1996/97. "Some replenishment of cereal stocks could occur," it added.
However it added that after last season's reduction, cereal reserves would remain well below minimum safe levels.
